chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from one of his men, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was digging the trench, they came across a rock. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took the pickaxe from the hand of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), or from the hand of Salman (may Allah be pleased with him). He struck it with a blow, and it split into three pieces. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The treasures of Kisra and Caesar have been opened up for me with this strike of mine.' One of them said to his companion: 'He promises us with the treasures of Kisra and Caesar, yet none of us can control his own need to go out for relieving himself.'

key_terms.الْخَنْدَق: The Trench, a defensive ditch dug by Muslims during the Battle of Khandaq
key_terms.قَيْصَرَ: Caesar, referring to the Roman Emperor
key_terms.كِسْرَى: Kisra, referring to the Persian Emperor (Khosrow)
key_terms.يَتَخَلَّى: To relieve oneself / go to the toilet

ai.seo_question: What happened when the Prophet struck the rock during the digging of the Trench?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophet's spiritual foresight during the Battle of the Trench, where a single strike with the pickaxe revealed the future dominion of the Persian and Roman empires. While the primary narration emphasizes the divine promise of worldly power and treasure, the appended humorous remark by a companion underscores the stark contrast between these grand eschatological visions and the immediate, humble realities of the early Muslim community's daily life.

en.hubeali: H 14712 – Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abaan Bin Usmaan, from one of his men, from Abu Abdullah having said:

When the Rasool Allahsaww dug the trench (Al-Khandaq), hesaww came across a rock. So the Rasool Allahsaww took a pickaxe from the hand of Amir-ul-Momineenasws, or from the hand of Salmanar. Hesaww struck by it at the rock and it split into three pieces. The Rasool Allahsaww said: ‘With this strike the treasures of Chosroe and Caesar have opened up for mesaww. So one of them (Abu Bakr or Umar) said to his companion, ‘Hesaww promises us with the treasures of Chosroe and Caesar whilst no one of us has the control to go out for the toilet’.
en.sarwar: 264. Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abaan Bin Usmaan, from one of his men, from Abu Abdullah having said:

When the Rasool Allah (saww) dug the trench (Al-Khandaq), he (saww) came across a rock. So the Rasool Allah (saww) took a pickaxe from the hand of Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.), or from the hand of Salman (ar). He (saww) struck by it at the rock and it split into three pieces. The Rasool Allah (saww) said: ‘With this strike the treasures of Chosroe and Caesar have opened up for me (saww). So one of them (Abu Bakr or Umar) said to his companion, ‘He (saww) promises us with the treasures of Chosroe and Caesar whilst no one of us has the control to go out for the toilet’.
